_THIS_IS_A_TEMPLATE: You are reading the blank template that 'deepmark-benchmark --init detection_reliability' prints. It is deliberately empty. Do NOT edit or run this file - edit your own copy at configs/detection_reliability.json, which is what --config takes.
_file: Reliability mode: does the detector fire when it should and stay quiet when it should not? False positive = a watermark reported in clean audio; false negative = a real watermark missed. Keys starting with _ are comments and are ignored. Reset with 'deepmark-benchmark --init detection_reliability'.
_mode: Which mode this file configures. One of: benchmark, no_attacks, detection_reliability.
_not_here: No ber metric in this mode: each file is scored detected/not-detected, so there are no payload bits to disagree - naming it is an error. crop_before_attack and comparison are not valid keys here either.
_general: Operational settings; the matching CLI flag overrides each one. wav_files_dir has no default - set it here or pass --wav_files_dir. report_dir is DELETED at the start of every run. save_audio also writes the attacked-clean files, which is how you listen to what caused a false positive.
_models: Exactly ONE model, which must implement is_watermarked() - listing more is an error. Zero-bit and confidence-based models qualify: PerthModel, AudioSealModel, AwareModel (others need the method added).
_attacks: groups and list are combined; leaving BOTH empty measures the no-attack baseline only (it does NOT mean all attacks here). groups - any of: process_disruption, audio_editing, audio_distortion, desynchronization, ai_attacks, transmission. list - attack class names, optionally AttackName:version. Every attack runs TWICE per file here (once on clean, once on watermarked), so a full set costs about double what benchmark mode costs.
_attacks_available: Attack class names for attacks.list, all 47 of them: AdditiveNoiseAttack, BandstopFilterAttack, ChorusAttack, Codec2VocoderAttack, Collusion2Attack, CollusionAttack, CropBeginningAttack, CropRandomAttack, CrossModelAttack, CutSamplesAttack, DescriptAudioCodecAttack, DiffusionAttack, EchoAttack, EncodecAttack, EqualizerAttack, FlangerAttack, FlipSamplesAttack, GaussianNoiseAttack, HighpassFilterAttack, InvertedTimeStretchAttack, LPCAttack, LowpassFilterAttack, MixingAttack, Mp3CompressionAttack, NetworkTransmissionAttack, NeuralVocoderAttack, OpusCodecAttack, PCMQuantizationAttack, PinkNoiseAttack, PitchShiftAttack, QuantizationAttack, Replacement2Attack, ReplacementAttack, ReplayAttack, ResamplingPolyAttack, STFTQuantizationAttack, SameModelAttack, SignInversionAttack, SmoothingAttack, SpeechEnhancement1Attack, SpeechEnhancement2Attack, SpeechTokenizationAttack, TimeStretchAttack, VAEAttack, WaveletAttack, ZeroBitCollusionAttack, ZeroCrossInsertsAttack.
_attacks_versions: No shipped attack declares parameter presets: each plugin's config.json holds one parameter set, which is its default version. You can define your own under attack_parameters as AttackName:version - give ALL of that attack's parameters, then name it in attacks.list. Naming an attack without a version runs every version it has. Codec2VocoderAttack expands to one run per bitrate in bitrate_codec2.
_attack_parameters: Override plugin parameters, keyed by attack CLASS NAME for its default version, or AttackName:version to define and configure a named one - e.g. {"GaussianNoiseAttack": {"snr_db_gaussian_noise": 25}, "GaussianNoiseAttack:mild": {"snr_db_gaussian_noise": 55}}, where :mild is a version this file defines. A bare name touches ONLY the default version, never the named ones.
_attack_parameters_new_version: Naming a version the plugin does not have DEFINES it, if you give ALL of that attack's parameters - it is then selectable in attacks.list and included when the attack is named without a version. Give only some and the entry is skipped with a warning, since the rest would silently come from the default preset.
_attack_parameters_checks: The attack name, every parameter name and every value type are checked against that plugin's config.json before the run starts. Find the parameter names with: cat src/deepmarkpy/plugins/attacks/<dir>/config.json

attack_parameters._example: Delete the underscore from a key below to activate it. The parser ignores every _-prefixed key, so this block is inert as written.

_calculate_quality_metrics: Master switch: true = the metrics block below decides what runs; false or absent = only pesq, visqol, stoi, and the enabled flags are IGNORED (statistics still apply). The quality tables describe the audio the detector was asked to judge, which separates a false negative caused by real damage from a fragile detector.
_statistics: Default statistics per metric, and the report column order. Any of: mean, std, median, p5, p10, p95, p99, worst_case. Delete this key to get all eight. FP/FN are counts over attempts, not distributions, so no statistic applies to them.
_metrics: Per metric: enabled (true/false) and statistics (a subset of the list above). Metrics - accuracy (always on, cannot be disabled), emr (a count, takes NO statistics), pesq, psnr, si_sdr, mcd, visqol, stoi, sii, ncm, nisqa_mos, nisqa_noi, nisqa_dis, nisqa_col, nisqa_loud. There is no ber in this mode. A metric named nowhere is off.

metrics._defaults: Baseline for every group. The signal metrics are OFF here and each group below switches on the ones that are meaningful for it, so a group section reads as a positive list of what it reports. accuracy/ber/emr are free (all three come from the accuracy array) and apply everywhere.
metrics._per_group: Each group lists the metrics it reports, as true. Inheritance is PER METRIC, so a group inherits anything it does not name from defaults above - where the signal metrics are off, which is why each section is a complete list. Group keys: the six attack families, then frequency_filtering / temporal_editing / audio_effects / compression_quantization (report subsections of audio_editing, NOT selectable in attacks.groups), then other. A group this run does not use is ignored; a MISSPELLED one is an error.

per_group._process_disruption: Collusion and re-watermarking keep the signal intact, so every metric applies.
per_group._audio_editing: The family as a whole. Its four subsections below are read INSTEAD of this in the detailed report, and each states its own full list because it inherits from here.
per_group._audio_distortion: Additive noise. No mcd: index-aligned, and it adds nothing PESQ and ViSQOL do not already say.
per_group._desynchronization: The time axis moves, so only mcd, visqol and the reference-free NISQA survive; the sample-aligned ones would report the shift as damage.
per_group._ai_attacks: Neural resynthesis rewrites the waveform, so psnr and si_sdr collapse while perceptual quality holds.
per_group._transmission: Replay and network loss keep sample alignment, so every metric applies.
per_group._frequency_filtering: audio_editing subsection: lowpass, highpass, bandstop, equalizer. psnr/si_sdr off.
per_group._temporal_editing: audio_editing subsection: cut, crop-beginning, crop-random. Signal length changes, so nothing can be compared to the original; accuracy, ber and emr still are.
per_group._audio_effects: audio_editing subsection: wavelet, smoothing, chorus, flanger, echo, mixing. psnr off.
per_group._compression_quantization: audio_editing subsection: quantization, MP3, Encodec, DAC, Opus, Codec2, resampling. si_sdr off.
per_group._other: Attacks in no declared family, including third-party plugins. Everything on, since nothing is known to be misleading.

_efficiency: What the run cost in TIME, kept apart from the metrics block above. Those describe the watermarking method and reproduce from a seed; these describe this machine on this day and do not. enabled: false means no timing is taken at all. Metrics - embed_latency, detect_latency, attack_latency (seconds). Memory and any later efficiency measure will be listed here too.
_efficiency_caveat: A native attack is timed as pure computation; one running in Docker includes base64 encoding of the audio and the HTTP round trip, so the two are not comparable. The first call to a cold container also pays for loading the model.

metrics._container_footprint: Resident memory of the model's container while warm, in MiB, read once per run via the docker CLI. It is the WHOLE service - weights, Python runtime, web server - not the size of the model, and the services load their weights at start so a container can never be measured empty. Absent, and simply omitted, when docker is unavailable or no container publishes the model's port.

_duration_groups: Report separately per audio length, which is how you see a detector whose false-positive rate climbs on short clips. boundaries: ascending seconds, e.g. [5, 10, 20, 30] gives <5s, 5-10s, 10-20s, 20-30s, >30s; an empty list disables grouping. include_overall adds a final all-files section.
